t:
Section 815 of title 10, United States Code (article 15 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), is amended—
    (1) in subsection (b)—
        (A) in paragraph (2)(A), by striking “on bread and water or diminished rations”; and 
        (B) in the undesignated matter after paragraph (2), by striking “on bread and water or diminished rations” in the sentence beginning “No two or more”; and  
    (2) in subsection (d), by striking “on bread and water or diminished rations” in paragraphs (2) and (3).

fable.w: This section only makes textual amendments to Article 15 of the UCMJ, removing references to confinement on bread and water or diminished rations. One might be tempted to see a procedural dimension because nonjudicial punishment is involved, but the section sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government.
fable.s: by striking “on bread and water or diminished rations”

qwen_block.w: This section amends the Uniform Code of Military Justice to remove specific punitive measures (bread and water or diminished rations). It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government. The text is purely legislative amendment regarding military discipline.
qwen_block.s: Section 815 of title 10, United States Code (article 15 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), is amended— (1) in subsection (b)— (A) in paragraph (2)(A), by striking “on bread and water or diminished rations”; and (B) in the undesignated matter after paragraph (2), by striking “on bread and water or diminished rations” in the sentence beginning “No two or more”; and (2) in subsection (d), by striking “on bread and water or diminished rations” in paragraphs (2) and (3).

opus.w: This amendment removes confinement "on bread and water or diminished rations" from the punishments allowed under Article 15 of the UCMJ. It does not involve anyone outside the federal government in any federal decision. The fact that Article 15 deals with disciplinary proceedings does not make it participation, because the text creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation or right to sue, and military members are federal personnel in any case.
opus.b:
**Step 1, the tempting reading:** Article 15 covers nonjudicial punishment, which involves proceedings and rights for the accused. That could make this look procedural. But the amendment only deletes the phrase "on bread and water or diminished rations" from the list of allowed punishments. It sets up no hearing, comment period, consultation or right to sue. Any service members involved are inside the federal government anyway.

**Step 2, the label:**

qwen_chat.w: This section amends the Uniform Code of Military Justice regarding permissible punishments for service members. Service members are federal employees, which places them inside the federal government boundary defined in the instructions. The text contains no requirement for consultation with, or participation by, any outside parties such as the public, states, or non-federal experts. It is a substantive change to internal military regulations, not a procedural requirement for external participation.
qwen_chat.s: Section 815 of title 10, United States Code (article 15 of the Uniform Code of Military Justice), is amended— (1) in subsection (b)— (A) in paragraph (2)(A), by striking “on bread and water or diminished rations”; and (B) in the undesignated matter after paragraph (2), by striking “on bread and water or diminished rations” in the sentence beginning “No two or more”; and (2) in subsection (d), by striking “on bread and water or diminished rations” in paragraphs (2) and (3).
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing military justice rules affects service members (who are federal employees) and thus involves "participation" if interpreted broadly as affecting people. However, the definition explicitly states that federal employees are INSIDE the federal government, and participation requires interaction with people OUTSIDE the government. This section merely amends statutory text regarding punishment limits; it does not create a process for outside consultation, public comment, or advisory input.
